domain_label: Turlock Ethnic Markets & Grocers — Market, Demand & Saturation Economics
purpose: A method for sizing and reading the Turlock independent ethnic-grocery market: quantifying the demand base (the four stacked immigrant communities — Hispanic/Latino, Assyrian, Portuguese/Azorean, and Punjabi/South-Asian & Afghan — plus the thin CSU Stanislaus secondary layer), explaining why the catalog holds ~10 stores and not 4 or 20, mapping the competitive structure across the five sub-categories (Assyrian/Middle-Eastern market, halal market, Mexican mercado/carniceria, Punjabi/South-Asian grocer, tortilleria), tracing the two-direction basket leakage to chains and to Modesto/online, locating the contested white-space, and expressing every revenue, margin and market-size figure strictly as a labeled benchmark estimate (industry benchmark x observable size signal) rather than as a stated fact for any named business.
assumptions: no per-business revenue dataset is supplied; every dollar figure is a labeled benchmark estimate, never an actual reported figure for any named business such as La Perla Tapatia or Shah Groceries
the universe is the 10 verified Turlock independent ethnic markets in businesses.json (chains excluded), as of the 2026-06-30 snapshot, and the count is read as a floor not a ceiling
city/county/state and community-demographic figures (population, income, ancestry shares, the ~20k Assyrian community estimate) are cited public facts or explicitly labeled derivations/estimates

sub-category revenue bands are published grocery/meat/bakery benchmarks (revenue per store / per sqft / per meat-department / net margin) scaled by an observable size signal (meat counter, bakery, prepared-food line, multi-department footprint), tagged estimate-not-actual with a confidence level and a confirmation path
Modesto (~218k pop, ~15 miles north) and national online ethnic-grocery/halal delivery are the out-of-town leakage anchors that skim the deep-specialty tail of the basket
the single highest-leverage confirmation for the uncertain dollar figures is CDTFA / Turlock Finance retail sales-tax receipts plus per-business CDFA/PFR licensure lookups
exclusions: per-store input sourcing, distributor links, cold-chain and meat-cutting operations — covered by the supply-chain KB
per-format unit-economics, cost-structure and go/no-go business-model detail — covered by the business-models KB
any claim of an actual, reported, or audited dollar revenue, margin, or square footage for a named business
chain supermarkets (Walmart, FoodMaxx) and franchise grocery, which are outside the independents-only catalog except as the leakage price floor
individual SKU assortment, shelf pricing tactics, or marketing execution for a specific operator

competency_questions.question: What is the demand base that sustains Turlock's ethnic-grocery sector, and how do the four stacked communities and the thin CSU layer feed it?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: DEMAND_BASE names the ~72,888 resident base and $82,995 median income; STACKED_COMMUNITIES ties each of the four communities (Hispanic 46.1%, Assyrian ~20k community estimate, Portuguese 7.3%, Punjabi/South-Asian & Afghan) to the formats it anchors; SECONDARY_DEMAND_LAYER gives the ~8,400 CSU students as a thin price-sensitive add-on

competency_questions.question: How does the stacking of four concentrated communities raise the store count above what population alone predicts?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: STACKED_COMMUNITIES explains the per-community over-index, citing the ~20k Assyrian estimate carrying three Middle-Eastern markets and the 46.1% Hispanic base carrying multiple carnicerias plus a tortilleria

competency_questions.question: How do format straddles (La Perla as carniceria + panaderia + tortilleria; Shah as grocer + halal butcher; Turlock Halal Market as halal + South-Asian) change the effective coverage of each sub-category?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: FORMAT_STRADDLE_MAP names the specific straddles and explains why effective coverage of halal butchering and tortilla output is larger than the primary-category tally implies

competency_questions.question: How is a sub-category benchmark revenue band built so it is an honest estimate and never a stated fact for a named business?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: BENCHMARK_METHOD states the benchmark x size-signal method, and SUBCATEGORY_REVENUE_BANDS gives the per-sub-category bands tagged estimate-not-actual with confidence and a confirmation path

competency_questions.question: What are the labeled benchmark revenue bands per sub-category, and why is high gross never high net?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: SUBCATEGORY_REVENUE_BANDS gives the per-sub-category bands and THIN_NET_MARGIN_REALITY pairs every band with the ~1-3% net caveat and the family-labor distortion

competency_questions.question: Why is the La Perla Tapatia multi-department band the single most uncertain figure in the analysis, and how must it be handled?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: LA_PERLA_OUTLIER_BAND states the ~$2M-$5M+ band as the lowest-confidence figure (footprint UNKNOWN), keeps the estimate tag prominent, and forbids it migrating into prose as fact

competency_questions.question: Why does Turlock sustain roughly 10 ethnic markets — not 4, not 20 — and what raises and caps that count?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: SATURATION_WHY_TEN names the ceiling-raiser (four stacked communities) and the four binding caps (per-community demand ceiling, two-direction leakage, licensing barrier stack, thin net margins) and ties the ~10 count to them

competency_questions.question: What is the sector density and why is ~1.37 stores per 10k high rather than low for one narrow segment?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: DENSITY_READ gives the 10/72,888 = ~1.37 per-10k figure as an estimate on FACT inputs, benchmarks it against USDA-ERS grocer density, and explains why it is high for one narrow ethnic sub-segment

competency_questions.question: Where is true saturation, and why is the Assyrian sub-category the one place a genuine demand ceiling binds?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: ASSYRIAN_SUBCAT_CEILING explains that three Middle-Eastern markets are likely at the ceiling for a ~20k community that also shops chains, and PER_COMMUNITY_DEMAND_CEILING generalizes the per-community ceiling logic across sub-categories

competency_questions.question: How does the basket leak in two directions — commodity half to chains, deep-specialty tail out of town — and what stays?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: COMMODITY_LEAKAGE_CHAINS explains the staple-basket leak to Walmart/FoodMaxx and the ~5-10% identical-goods cost disadvantage, and SPECIALTY_LEAKAGE_OUTOFTOWN explains the deep-specialty leak to Modesto and online, leaving only the specialty middle

competency_questions.question: Where is the defensible profit, and what is the moat that chains and Amazon cannot replicate?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: SPECIALTY_MOAT names in-house production (masa, sweets, bakery, prepared foods), fresh in-house meat, halal credibility, and in-language trust as the chain-proof parts of the basket, citing La Perla, Shah, Nineveh, Tres Hermanos

competency_questions.question: How is an entry verdict reached for adding a store, what licensing/leakage gate overrides a demand-true opening, and how are the reads refreshed when the figures change?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: MARKET_ENTRY_VERDICT composes the saturation read, the contested white-space rank, the licensing barrier stack and leakage into a verdict that refuses a fourth Assyrian market or a center-of-town carniceria and gates demand-true openings; MARKET_REVIEW_LOOP defines the refresh cadence and the material-change triggers (CDTFA receipts, migration shift, demographic refresh, licensure lookup) that re-run sizing and saturation

glossary.definition: Turlock's defining demand feature: four distinct, concentrated immigrant communities (Hispanic/Latino 46.1%, an estimated ~20,000-person Assyrian community, Portuguese/Azorean 7.3% ancestry, and a rising Punjabi/South-Asian & Afghan segment) each demanding a format chains underserve, stacking to support ~10 ethnic markets a generic 73k town would not carry.

The honest revenue-estimation method used throughout: take a published grocery/meat/bakery benchmark (revenue per store, per sqft, per meat-department, net margin) and scale it by an observable Turlock size signal (meat counter present? bakery? prepared food? multi-department?), yielding a band tagged estimate-not-actual with a confidence level — never a stated dollar fact for a named business.

The mechanism that caps the sector: the commodity half of the basket (masa, produce, rice, bulk meat) leaks in-town to Walmart/FoodMaxx at a price floor independents cannot beat (they pay ~5-10% more for identical goods), while the deep-specialty tail leaks out of town to Modesto and to national online ethnic-grocery/halal delivery; independents keep only the specialty middle.

The defensible core — specialty SKUs, fresh in-house meat, halal credibility, in-language trust, and in-house production (masa at Tres Hermanos/La Perla, sweets at Shah, bakery at Nineveh/La Perla, prepared foods at La Rancherita) — the parts of the basket that do not leak to a chain or to Amazon and where the thin profit actually sits.

The cap a single concentrated community places on how many dedicated stores it can sustain while also shopping chains; three Assyrian/Middle-Eastern markets is likely at the ceiling for a ~20k community, the one sub-category where genuine saturation exists, while a rising community (Punjabi/South-Asian) still has demand-side headroom.

The real permit stack that prices out casual dry-goods-only entrants: county retail food permit + plan check, CDFA retail meat-processing licensure (on-site inspector when making product), CDPH Processed Food Registration for packaged/wholesale output, CDFA Weighmaster/device registration for scales, and — for halal — a private certifier chain-of-custody; a cited regime whose binding effect is an estimate.

A per-capita density read: 10 catalogued ethnic markets / 72,888 residents = ~1.37 per 10,000, an estimate on FACT inputs; benchmarked against USDA-ERS grocer density (>3 independent grocers per 10k is 91% remote-rural; NY peaks ~4.3 all-format per 10k), ~1.37 for one narrow ethnic sub-segment reads as high, since most towns carry near-zero dedicated ethnic grocers.

An under-served format where real unmet demand exists but the supply side is partially pre-empted: Punjabi/South-Asian grocery (one dedicated grocer, Shah, plus halal overlap) is the clearest demand-side opening, yet it is precisely where Modesto and national online delivery leak hardest, so an entrant competes against out-of-town and online options, not an empty field.

The discipline that '10 businesses' is the count this catalog confirms, not a claim that no eleventh ethnic grocer operates in Turlock; small, newly opened, single-listing, home-based or pop-up halal/South-Asian sellers and edge-of-town carnicerias may be undercounted, so density and saturation conclusions are read as at-least statements.

The binding honesty discipline: per-business revenue, margin and square footage are not public, so no dollar figure is ever stated as an actual reported figure for a named business; every band is a labeled benchmark estimate carrying its method, public source and confidence, every high-gross band is paired with the ~1-3% thin-net caveat, and supplier/licensure links are representative inference unless a cited source states otherwise.

source_registry.description: labeled benchmark estimates and cited public facts for the Turlock independent ethnic-grocery market, grounded in the ethnic_markets deep-dive (DEEPDIVE.md), its reconciled brief (reconciled.md), and the 10-business source dataset (businesses.json); demand sizing uses census/ACS community shares and grocery-spend benchmarks, sub-category revenue bands use published grocery/meat-department/bakery benchmarks scaled by observable size signals, and density/saturation reads use census population and USDA-ERS grocers-per-capita figures
source_registry.citation_or_locator: california-demographics 2024 (Turlock ~72,888 pop, $82,995 median HH income, median age 34.9, 46.1% Hispanic, 7.3% Portuguese ancestry, ~6.1% Assyrian ancestry); Census Reporter/USAFacts (Stanislaus 50.0% Hispanic); KQED / fredaprim.com (~20,000 Assyrian community estimate, NOT a Census line); CSU Stanislaus enrollment (~8,400 students); USDA ERS grocers-per-10k bands; published grocery/meat/bakery benchmarks (VantaInsights, itRetail, PlanPros, Toast, FinancialModelsLab); CDTFA / Turlock Finance retail sales-tax categories and CDFA/PFR licensure lookups (the confirmation sources); ethnic_markets DEEPDIVE.md, reconciled.md, businesses.json

nodes.definition: Catalog the structural resident demand base the ten ethnic markets share: a ~72,888 Turlock population (FACT — california-demographics 2024) with a $82,995 median household income and a median age of 34.9, sitting inside Stanislaus County. Grocery demand here is essential, high-frequency, partly counter-cyclical (households trade down into bulk staples in downturns) and 100% out-of-pocket cash with no third-party payer, so margins live on volume and shrink control, not reimbursement. This resident base, not its raw size, is the floor the sector reads against — what makes Turlock fertile is not population but the communities stacked on top of it.

included: resident population, median income, median age
the essential/counter-cyclical cash-demand character of grocery
excluded: the community stacking that anchors formats (its own node)
converting the base into a dollar pool

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a population, income, or age figure is refreshed

pros.claim: Establishing an essential, cash, high-frequency demand floor explains why the sector is more resilient than discretionary retail
pros.example: households trading down into bulk staples in a downturn cushions carniceria/grocery volume where a restaurant would lose covers

cons.claim: A raw resident count badly under-predicts the count without the community overlay, so the base alone misleads
cons.example: a generic 73k town reads as supporting 2-4 ethnic markets, not the ~10 Turlock carries

failure_modes: sizing demand on population alone and concluding the sector is over-built
treating grocery demand as discretionary like dining and over-stating downturn risk
acceptance_tests: the resident base is stated with its public-fact magnitudes (pop ~72,888, median income $82,995, median age 34.9) and the essential/cash/counter-cyclical demand character is named with its source confidence
revisit_triggers: a census or ACS demographic refresh
a median-income or population release
a macro downturn that tests the counter-cyclical read

nodes.definition: Explain the sector's defining demand feature: four distinct, concentrated communities each anchor a chain-proof format. The Hispanic/Latino base (46.1% of Turlock, 50.0% of Stanislaus County) is the deep daily-shopper base for the Mexican mercado/carniceria and tortilleria, carrying La Morenita, La Rancherita, La Perla and Tres Hermanos. The Assyrian community — ~6.1% by Census ancestry but a community/press estimate of ~20,000 (~a quarter of town, 'Little Urmia'; a hedged community figure, NOT a Census line) — independently carries three Middle-Eastern markets (International Bazar, Neesan, Nineveh). The Portuguese/Azorean 7.3% ancestry overlaps the specialty-bakery demand (Nineveh's bakery). The rising Punjabi/South-Asian & Afghan/Middle-Eastern segment, smaller but growing, carries Shah and the halal overlap. This stacking is why Turlock over-indexes per capita on ethnic independents.

included: the four community shares and the ~20k Assyrian estimate
excluded: the dollar size of each community's spend

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a community share or migration trend changes

pros.claim: Mapping each community to its anchored sub-category explains a count national density models under-predict
pros.example: a ~20k Assyrian community independently sustaining three Middle-Eastern markets makes sense only against the hedged community estimate, not the 6.1% Census line

cons.claim: Ancestry share is a crude proxy for grocery spend, and the load-bearing ~20k Assyrian figure is a community estimate not a Census line
cons.example: the three-Assyrian-market read is only as solid as the hedged ~20k figure it rests on

failure_modes: assuming ancestry share converts linearly to store revenue
quoting the ~20,000 Assyrian figure as a Census fact rather than a hedged community estimate
acceptance_tests: each of the four communities is tied to at least one anchored sub-category with its cited share, and the ~20,000 Assyrian figure carries the explicit community-estimate hedge
revisit_triggers: an ancestry/demographic data refresh
a community grows or contracts via migration
the Assyrian community estimate is re-sourced or revised

nodes.definition: Isolate the thin secondary demand layer CSU Stanislaus adds: roughly 8,400 students who are a price-sensitive, term-time add-on rather than a primary driver. They lift snack, halal-option and prepared-food demand at the margin (the shawarma/kabob line at Halal Market and Food, juice/snack bar at Shah, hot food at La Rancherita) but do not anchor any sub-category the way the four communities do, and their demand carries an academic-calendar dip in summer and over breaks. Treat this layer as a real but bounded supplement that should never be mistaken for a structural demand engine on the scale of the Hispanic or Assyrian base.

excluded: the cultural-calendar seasonality of the communities (folded into other nodes)

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a CSU enrollment or commuter-pattern figure changes

pros.claim: Bounding the student layer prevents over-crediting it as a primary demand engine
pros.example: marking CSU as a marginal prepared-food/snack lift stops a would-be entrant building a store on student traffic that empties each summer

cons.claim: A thin, calendar-fragile layer is easy to ignore entirely, missing its real prepared-food and halal lift
cons.example: discounting students fully understates the hot-food and halal-snack pull at the campus-adjacent end

failure_modes: treating peak-term student traffic as year-round baseline
elevating the student layer to a primary anchor on the level of the four communities
acceptance_tests: the ~8,400 CSU figure is stated, tied to the specific prepared-food/halal/snack lift, and explicitly bounded as a thin price-sensitive secondary layer with an academic-calendar dip
revisit_triggers: a CSU enrollment release moves the figure
a campus-housing or commuter change shifts daypart demand

nodes.definition: Map the format straddles that make the five primary sub-categories (Assyrian/Middle-Eastern market 3, halal market 2, Mexican mercado/carniceria 3, Punjabi/South-Asian grocer 1, tortilleria 1) understate true coverage. La Perla Tapatia is simultaneously a carniceria, a panaderia and a tortilleria; Shah Groceries is a South-Asian grocer and a full halal butcher and a sweets/juice operation; Turlock Halal Market is a halal market and a Punjabi/South-Asian grocer; Nineveh adds a European/specialty bakery; Halal Market and Food adds a shawarma/kabob food-service line. The effective coverage of, for example, halal butchering and daily tortilla output is therefore larger than the 2-store halal or 1-store tortilleria tally implies — a fact that matters for every saturation read downstream.

included: the named primary/secondary straddles per business
why effective coverage exceeds the primary tally

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a business's primary/secondary format mix changes

pros.claim: Surfacing straddles prevents under-counting effective coverage of halal meat and tortilla output
pros.example: counting only the 2 halal markets misses Shah's full halal counter, so halal butchering coverage is effectively three-plus stores

cons.claim: Double-listing a business under two formats can instead inflate an apparent saturation count if not spine-controlled
cons.example: tallying La Perla under carniceria and tortilleria and panaderia triple-counts one storefront

failure_modes: counting only primary categories and under-stating halal/tortilla coverage
double-counting a straddle business and over-stating a sub-category's saturation
acceptance_tests: the specific straddles for La Perla, Shah, Turlock Halal Market, Nineveh and Halal Market and Food are named, and the spine-is-primary-category convention is stated so straddles adjust but do not double-count the saturation read
revisit_triggers: a business adds or drops a secondary format
a new straddle business enters the catalog

nodes.definition: Define the honest revenue-estimation method that governs every dollar figure: method = published industry benchmark (grocery revenue per store, revenue per sqft, meat-department gross per ~2k sqft, net margin) multiplied by an observable Turlock size signal inferred from businesses.json offering descriptions (meat counter present? bakery? prepared-food line? multi-department footprint?). Confidence reflects how well a format benchmark maps to an unknown local footprint. The cost-structure backbone applied sector-wide is published: grocery COGS ~70-75% (gross margin ~25-30%), meat-department gross ~25-45%, labor ~15-20% of revenue (understated by uncompensated family labor), net ~1-3% base case. No dollar revenue is ever stated for any named business; the size signal is the only local input and it is itself inferred, not measured.

excluded: the specific per-sub-category band values (their own node)

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a benchmark source or measured size signal changes

pros.claim: A transparent benchmark x size-signal method yields a defensible band without quoting any business
pros.example: a meat-counter carniceria band built from published meat-department gross x an observed counter is auditable and business-agnostic

cons.claim: The size signal is inferred from offering text, not measured, so any single store can sit far outside its band
cons.example: an unobserved large footprint could push a store well above the band its offering description implies

failure_modes: presenting a benchmark-derived band as a measured figure
dropping the published-backbone caveats so a high-gross meat band reads as high profit
acceptance_tests: the method is stated as published-benchmark x observable-size-signal, the COGS ~70-75% / meat gross ~25-45% / net ~1-3% backbone is given, and every output is tagged estimate-not-actual with a confidence and confirmation path
revisit_triggers: a published grocery/meat/bakery benchmark updates
an observable size signal (footprint, departments) is measured for a store
CDTFA distribution data lands

nodes.definition: Build the per-sub-category revenue bands that are the primary, most defensible revenue view, every one a labeled estimate (published benchmark x observable size signal), never an actual figure for a named business. Representative bands: Assyrian/Middle-Eastern market (International Bazar, Neesan, Nineveh) ~$400k-$1.1M/yr each, dry-goods COGS ~70-75%, no fresh-meat engine, bakery/gift attach lifts the top; halal market (Halal Market and Food, Turlock Halal Market) ~$350k-$900k/yr each, the food-service unit skewing higher on prepared-food uplift; Mexican mercado/carniceria (La Morenita, La Rancherita) ~$700k-$1.6M/yr each on the meat-counter format and largest Hispanic base; Punjabi/South-Asian grocer (Shah) ~$600k-$1.4M/yr on grocer + meat + sweets attach; tortilleria (Tres Hermanos) ~$150k-$600k/yr, volume-driven with a wholesale swing factor. Each pairs revenue with its cost/margin reality so high gross is never read as high net.

excluded: the La Perla multi-department outlier band (its own node)

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a benchmark source or measured size signal changes

pros.claim: Per-sub-category bands anchored to published benchmarks give a planning estimate without quoting any operator
pros.example: a carniceria band of ~$700k-$1.6M from meat-department gross x an observed counter is auditable and business-agnostic

cons.claim: Bands rest on national benchmarks and inferred size signals, so any single store can sit far outside its band, and the wholesale swing widens the tortilleria band
cons.example: Tres Hermanos' band shifts materially upward if it sells B2B to taquerias, an unmodeled swing factor

failure_modes: attaching a band to a named business as if it were that business's revenue
dropping the cost/margin pairing so a high-gross meat format reads as high-profit
acceptance_tests: each of the five sub-categories has a band derived as benchmark x a stated size signal, tagged estimate-not-actual with confidence and a confirmation path, and paired with its cost/margin caveat
revisit_triggers: a published benchmark source updates
an observable size signal (footprint, meat dept, wholesale mix) is measured
CDTFA distribution data lands

nodes.definition: Pair every revenue band with the net-margin reality so high gross is never mistaken for high profit. Independent small grocers run ~1-3% net (base case); specialty/ethnic differentiators can reach ~5-6%; the 8-12% figure some sources cite is an operating-margin/aspirational number, NOT net, and must never be quoted as net. Even the meat counter's richer 25-45% gross does not lift net, because owner draw and thin grocery margins absorb most of it. Family-labor distortion bends every figure: owner/family labor is often uncompensated or drawn as profit, so book labor % understates real labor and book net overstates true economic margin. The formula net_band_low = gross_margin_pct - opex_pct holds only directionally; the binding read is ~1-3% net across the sector.

included: the 1-3% net base case and 5-6% differentiator ceiling

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a net-margin benchmark or input-cost figure changes

pros.claim: Anchoring net at 1-3% stops a high meat-counter gross being read as high profit
pros.example: a 25-45% meat-department gross paired with the 1-3% net caveat prevents over-stating carniceria profitability

cons.claim: A single sector-wide net band hides genuine variation between a dry-goods importer and a vertically integrated supermarket
cons.example: a specialty differentiator at 5-6% and a commodity-leaning store near 1% are flattened into one band

failure_modes: quoting the 8-12% operating/aspirational figure as a net margin
reading the high meat-counter gross as high net without the owner-draw absorption
acceptance_tests: net is stated as ~1-3% base case with the 5-6% differentiator ceiling, the 8-12% figure is explicitly flagged operating-not-net, and the family-labor distortion is named as bending every labor and net figure
revisit_triggers: a grocery net-margin benchmark updates
operator data quantifies a real net for a sub-category
an input-cost shock moves COGS

nodes.definition: Handle La Perla Tapatia as the sector's revenue outlier and the single most uncertain figure in the analysis. It is a multi-department Mexican supermarket (meat market + panaderia + tortilleria + salsa bar + grocery), a family-owned chain headquartered in Turlock, and the most vertically integrated business in the sector. Its labeled benchmark band is ~$2M-$5M+ per year for this location, derived as revenue-per-sqft x a larger-but-UNKNOWN footprint, carrying the lowest confidence in the document because the footprint is not observed. The estimate tag must stay prominent wherever the band is reused; the '$2M-$5M+' must never migrate into prose as a stated fact, and the band must not be lumped with the single-store carniceria band.

excluded: the saturation read for the Mexican sub-category

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: La Perla footprint or scale data appears

pros.claim: Separating La Perla as an outlier prevents its multi-department scale distorting the single-store carniceria band
pros.example: lumping La Perla's ~$2M-$5M+ with La Morenita's ~$700k-$1.6M would inflate the typical carniceria read

cons.claim: The footprint is unobserved, so the band is the widest and least confident figure in the analysis
cons.example: without a measured square footage the $2M vs $5M endpoints differ by more than the band's own midpoint

failure_modes: letting '$2M-$5M+' migrate into prose as a stated fact for La Perla
averaging La Perla into the single-store carniceria band
acceptance_tests: the La Perla band is stated as ~$2M-$5M+ tagged the lowest-confidence estimate with footprint UNKNOWN, kept separate from the single-store carniceria band, and explicitly barred from migrating into prose as fact
revisit_triggers: La Perla's footprint or department count is measured
CDTFA receipts or a licensure lookup resolve its scale
a new La Perla location opens or closes

nodes.definition: Read the sector density: 10 catalogued ethnic markets / 72,888 residents = ~1.37 per 10,000 (estimate — arithmetic on FACT inputs). Because there is no clean national 'ethnic grocer per 10k' series, this triangulates against general grocery density: USDA-ERS shows counties with >3 independent grocers per 10k are 91% remote-rural, and even dense New York peaks at ~4.3 all-format grocery stores per 10k. Against that, ~1.37 per 10k for one narrow ethnic sub-segment is high, not low, because most towns of any size carry near-zero dedicated ethnic grocers; a generic 73k town would support perhaps 2-4 ethnic-leaning markets total (estimate, low-medium confidence). Turlock carries ~10 — demand-justified, not over-built.

excluded: why exactly ten and not twenty (its own node)

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: the catalog count or population figure changes

pros.claim: Benchmarking ~1.37/10k against USDA-ERS grocer density shows the count is high for one narrow segment, not a deficit
pros.example: most 73k towns carry near-zero dedicated ethnic grocers, so ~1.37 reads as over-index not under-supply

cons.claim: No clean ethnic-grocer-per-10k series exists, so the benchmark is a triangulation against all-format grocery density, not a like-for-like
cons.example: comparing one narrow ethnic segment to all-format NY density is directional, not exact

failure_modes: comparing ~1.37 to all-format grocery bands and wrongly concluding the sector is under-built
treating the ~1.37 as exact when the 10-count is a floor
acceptance_tests: the ~1.37 per-10k figure is derived from 10/72,888, benchmarked against the USDA-ERS bands, and explicitly read as high for one narrow ethnic sub-segment with the 2-4 generic-town counterfactual
revisit_triggers: the catalog count changes
a population refresh
a national ethnic-grocer density series becomes available

nodes.definition: Explain why Turlock sustains roughly 10 ethnic markets — not 4, not 20 — as the resolution of one ceiling-raiser against four binding caps. The raiser: four stacked communities each demand a chain-proof format, so the sector over-indexes (the Hispanic 46% base alone carries multiple carnicerias plus a tortilleria; the ~20k Assyrian base independently carries three Middle-Eastern markets). The four caps holding it to ~10: (1) a per-community demand ceiling (three Assyrian markets is likely at the ceiling); (2) two-direction basket leakage (commodity half to Walmart/FoodMaxx, deep-specialty tail to Modesto/online); (3) a real licensing/operational barrier stack (CDFA meat-processing, Weighmaster scales, PFR, halal certification); and (4) thin ~1-3% net margins that punish anyone winning on the leaky commodity half. Ten is demand-justified, not over-built.

excluded: the per-sub-category Assyrian ceiling detail (its own node)

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a cap or the stacking raiser shifts

pros.claim: Framing ten as a raiser-vs-four-caps equilibrium resists both over-building and under-building conclusions
pros.example: it explains why Turlock is neither a deficit (the raiser) nor a glut (the caps) at ~10 stores

cons.claim: An equilibrium framing can imply false stability when migration and chain/online leakage are moving
cons.example: treating ~10 as fixed when rising Punjabi/South-Asian immigration could lift the sustainable count

nodes.definition: Read the Assyrian/Middle-Eastern sub-category as the one place genuine saturation exists. Three markets (International Bazar, Neesan, Nineveh) split a defined ~20k-person base (itself a hedged community estimate) plus chain-shopping leakage, which is likely at the ceiling for a community of that size that also shops chains; a fourth would split, not grow, the pie. Differentiation is now by attach — Nineveh's bakery, Neesan's gifts — rather than by core grocery, and new entry is unlikely to pencil. This read rests entirely on the hedged ~20k figure; if that community estimate is lower, the three-market saturation conclusion weakens proportionally.

nodes.definition: Generalize the per-community demand-ceiling logic across the sector: each concentrated community can sustain only so many dedicated stores while also shopping chains, and that ceiling — not total population — is the binding cap on each sub-category. The Assyrian sub-category is at its ceiling at three; the Mexican mercado/carniceria is center-saturated (the town center is competitive, anchored by La Perla) but edge-open on the 46%-and-rising Hispanic base; the Punjabi/South-Asian community, smaller but rising, still has demand-side headroom (one dedicated grocer, Shah, plus halal overlap). The ceiling is dynamic: it moves with migration and county Hispanic share (48.1%->50.0%), so a sub-category at ceiling today can re-open as its anchoring community grows.

included: the per-community ceiling as the binding cap
the dynamic ceiling moving with migration
excluded: the Assyrian-specific saturation detail (its own node)

nodes.definition: Characterize the competitive structure: the ten are all verified independents with no chain dominance, consistent with the Ethnic Supermarkets industry being highly fragmented with no firm holding >5% share (FACT — IBISWorld). Competition is intra-community and format-specific rather than head-to-head across the whole sector: the three Assyrian markets compete with each other and with chain-shopping leakage; the carnicerias compete in the town center where La Perla is the toughest anchor; the halal and South-Asian stores compete with each other and with out-of-town/online options. La Perla should be read as an outlier anchor, not lumped with single-store carnicerias. The structural source of defensibility is vertical integration (in-house meat, bakery, tortilla, sweets, prepared food), which is what keeps competition specialty-led rather than price-led.

excluded: the leakage to chains and out-of-town (their own nodes)

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a store count or chain assortment change shifts competition

pros.claim: Framing competition as intra-community and format-specific avoids a false head-to-head whole-sector read
pros.example: an Assyrian market does not compete with a tortilleria; each faces its own community and leakage

cons.claim: Format-specific framing can understate cross-format competition for the same household's total grocery wallet
cons.example: a Hispanic household splits spend across a carniceria, a chain and a tortilleria, blurring the format lines

lumping La Perla's multi-department anchor with single-store carnicerias

revisit_triggers: a store opens or closes shifting a sub-category's competitive density
a chain expands its ethnic assortment

nodes.definition: Catalog the real permit and operational barrier stack that gates the sector and prices out casual dry-goods-only entrants (FACT — licensing regime; binding-effect ESTIMATE). Every store operates under a Stanislaus County retail food permit + plan check (California Retail Food Code). In-store meat counters that make product require CDFA retail meat-processing licensure with a Processing Inspector on site when product is being made, and resale meat must come from a USDA-inspected facility — applying to La Rancherita, La Morenita, La Perla and the halal markets' marinated meat. Packaged/house-made products sold beyond the counter (bagged tortillas, salsas, sweets) trigger CDPH Processed Food Registration (PFR), the gate that converts retail tortilla output into a wholesale lane. Every meat/deli scale needs CDFA Weighmaster/device registration. Halal credibility is not a state license but a private certifier chain-of-custody, operationally binding because community trust is the moat. Whether any named business currently holds CDFA/PFR licensure is UNKNOWN.

included: the county food permit, CDFA meat-processing, PFR, Weighmaster, and halal-certifier gates

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a permit, license, or certification fee or availability changes

cons.example: whether La Rancherita currently holds CDFA meat-processing licensure is not publicly verified

reading the barrier stack as a pure cost rather than also the entrant's eventual moat once cleared
acceptance_tests: the county food permit, CDFA retail meat-processing licensure, CDPH PFR, CDFA Weighmaster registration and the private halal certifier are each named as gates, with the per-business licensure status flagged UNKNOWN
revisit_triggers: a city/county/CDFA permit or PFR/halal-certification fee or availability changes

nodes.definition: Trace the first leakage direction: the commodity half of the basket (masa, produce, rice, bulk meat) leaks in-town to Walmart and FoodMaxx, which set a price floor independents cannot beat — independents pay an estimated 5-10% more for identical goods (estimate, medium confidence) than chains negotiate, a structural staple-basket disadvantage. This is why winning on the commodity basket is not viable for these stores and why thin net margins punish anyone who tries. The leakage is a mechanism with medium-confidence magnitude: the direction (staples leak to chains) is well-supported, but the exact share of each household's staple spend going to Walmart/FoodMaxx is UNKNOWN without local sales data.

excluded: the deep-specialty out-of-town leak (its own node)
the specialty moat that resists leakage

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a chain pricing or input-cost figure changes

pros.claim: Naming the commodity leak and the ~5-10% cost gap explains why independents cannot win on staples
pros.example: a chain price floor on rice and produce makes a staple-led independent unviable regardless of demand

cons.claim: The leak's magnitude is unmeasured, so only the direction is solid
cons.example: without local sales data the exact staple share going to Walmart vs the independent is UNKNOWN

failure_modes: treating the ~5-10% cost gap or the leak share as a measured figure
concluding independents can compete on the commodity basket if they cut price
acceptance_tests: the staple-basket leak to Walmart/FoodMaxx is stated with the ~5-10% identical-goods cost disadvantage as a medium-confidence estimate and the magnitude flagged UNKNOWN
revisit_triggers: a chain opens, closes, or changes ethnic assortment
a wholesale input-cost shift changes the ~5-10% gap
local sales data quantifies the leak

nodes.definition: Trace the second leakage direction: the deep-specialty tail of the basket leaks out of town. Modesto (~15 miles north, ~218k pop, FACT) carries larger ethnic supermarkets and a broader South-Asian/halal selection, and national online ethnic-grocery/halal-meat delivery skims small-volume shelf-stable imports. Between them, the deepest-specialty SKUs and the thinnest-volume imports leak away, leaving Turlock independents only the specialty middle of the basket — too specialized for the chains, not deep or niche enough to be worth a Modesto trip or an online order. The mechanism is medium-confidence; the magnitude is UNKNOWN without a cross-shop study. This leak is what makes the Punjabi/South-Asian white-space contested rather than open.

included: the national online ethnic/halal delivery skim
excluded: the commodity leak to chains (its own node)
the contested white-space ranking (its own node)

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: Modesto or online ethnic-grocery availability changes

pros.claim: Naming the out-of-town leak explains why deep-specialty demand does not translate into a viable local store
pros.example: a Punjabi household drives to Modesto or orders online for the deepest SKUs, capping a Turlock South-Asian grocer's range

cons.claim: Leakage to Modesto and online is inferred from proximity and scale, not measured
cons.example: without a cross-shop study the exact share of deep-specialty spend leaving Turlock is UNKNOWN

ignoring the leak and reading South-Asian demand as fully capturable locally

revisit_triggers: Modesto's ethnic-grocery scene expands or contracts
online ethnic/halal delivery coverage changes

nodes.definition: Locate the defensible profit: the moat is specialty + trust + in-house production, not commodity grocery. The parts of the basket these ten own — specialty SKUs, fresh in-house meat, masa, sweets, halal counters, in-language trust — are exactly the parts that do not leak to a chain or to Amazon. Value-added in-house production is the margin lift above resale: La Perla's bakery/tortilla/salsa, Shah's Indian sweets, Nineveh's European bakery, La Rancherita's carnitas/tamales/marinated meats, Tres Hermanos' from-scratch masa. Halal credibility (a private certifier chain-of-custody) and in-language trust are things chains cannot replicate. These ten are not displaced by Walmart because the specialty middle they own is precisely the part of the basket that stays.

included: in-house production as the margin lift
excluded: the entry verdict that uses the moat

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a chain/online entrant or skilled-labor shift threatens the moat

pros.claim: Naming the specialty/trust/in-house-production moat identifies exactly where defensible profit sits
pros.example: Tres Hermanos' from-scratch masa and Shah's sweets are margin lifts a chain cannot replicate

cons.claim: In-house production raises labor and equipment cost and skilled-labor dependence, so the moat is not free margin
cons.example: a panadero or halal cutter shortage can stall the very production that forms the moat

failure_modes: mistaking the high meat/bakery gross for free margin without the labor/equipment cost
assuming the moat holds without the skilled-labor (butcher, baker, tortilla operator) supply
acceptance_tests: the moat is named as specialty SKUs + fresh in-house meat + in-house production + halal credibility + in-language trust, tied to specific businesses (La Perla, Shah, Nineveh, La Rancherita, Tres Hermanos) as the chain-proof part of the basket
revisit_triggers: a chain begins replicating an in-house production line (fresh tortillas, halal counter)
a skilled-labor shortage threatens production
an online entrant captures a previously moated specialty

nodes.definition: Locate and qualify the white-space, marking each opening contested rather than open. (1) Punjabi/South-Asian grocery (one dedicated grocer, Shah, plus halal overlap) is the clearest demand-side white-space relative to a rising immigrant community, but it is precisely where Modesto and national online delivery leak hardest, so the supply side is partially pre-empted — real unmet demand, but not an empty field. (2) A standalone certified halal butcher reads more as an attach inside existing stores (as Shah and the halal markets already do) than as a viable standalone format. (3) Tortilleria B2B wholesale-to-foodservice (taquerias, restaurants) is an under-exploited lane that would shift a producer's band upward but requires clearing the CDPH PFR packaging/distribution gate. (4) Neighborhood carnicerias on the growing south/west edges remain viable on the 46%-and-rising Hispanic base. Each is demand-true but gated by leakage and/or the licensing barrier stack.

included: the attach-vs-standalone halal read and the PFR-gated wholesale lane
excluded: the licensing barrier stack detail (folded into the verdict node)
the per-decision entry verdict (its own node)

acceptance_tests: at least four white-space openings are listed, each with its demand basis and an explicit leakage and/or licensing-gate qualifier, and the halal-as-attach and PFR-gated wholesale reads are stated
revisit_triggers: a white-space format is entered locally

nodes.definition: Enforce the binding honesty discipline across every dollar figure: per-business revenue, margin and square footage are not public for these privately held independents, so no dollar figure is ever stated as an actual reported figure for a named business such as La Perla Tapatia or Shah Groceries. Every sub-category dollar band is a labeled benchmark estimate (published benchmark x observable size signal) tagged estimate-not-actual with method, public source, confidence and a confirmation path; every high-gross band is paired with its ~1-3% thin-net caveat; city/county/state and community figures are cited public facts or labeled derivations (the ~20k Assyrian figure keeps its community-estimate hedge); supplier-to-named-business links and per-business licensure are representative inference unless a cited source states otherwise; and coverage is reported as a floor, not a ceiling. This guardrail governs how all sizing, saturation and white-space nodes may be expressed.

included: the estimate-not-actual labeling rule (method + source + confidence travels with every number)
the public-fact-vs-hedged-estimate distinction and the coverage floor

nodes.definition: Encode the coverage discipline: '10 businesses' is the count this catalog confirms, not a claim that no eleventh ethnic grocer operates in Turlock. Small, newly opened, single-listing-only stores — especially neighborhood carnicerias on the growing south/west edges and home-based or pop-up halal/South-Asian sellers — may be undercounted, so every density and saturation conclusion is read as an at-least statement. This caveat caps how strongly the saturation reads (especially the demand-justified verdict and the per-community ceilings) can be asserted: the sector is at least this dense, the sub-categories are at least this covered, and a 'true saturation' call is a floor on competition, not a proof that no further store can open.

nodes.definition: Produce the market entry verdict for adding a given ethnic-market format, composing the saturation read, the per-community ceiling, the contested white-space rank, the two-direction leakage, the specialty moat and the licensing barrier stack into one decision. The merged rule: do not open a fourth Assyrian/Middle-Eastern market or a center-of-town carniceria (both at ceiling); the defensible headroom is Punjabi/South-Asian grocery, edge-of-town carnicerias, and PFR-gated tortilleria wholesale — each viable only on specialty/fresh-meat/in-house production (never the leaky commodity basket) and only after clearing the barrier stack (county food permit + plan check, CDFA retail meat-processing licensure with on-site inspector when making product, Weighmaster scale registration, PFR for packaged/wholesale output, and a halal certifier chain-of-custody). A demand-true opening that fails the leakage test or the licensing gate is a no-go until those clear.

recommending a commodity-basket-led store that the chain price floor dooms

revisit_triggers: a saturation read, leakage estimate, or licensing gate feeding the verdict changes

nodes.definition: Define the loop that keeps the market reads current. A fixed refresh cadence (re-run on each major data release) plus material-change triggers — new CDTFA / Turlock Finance retail sales-tax receipts and per-business CDFA/PFR licensure lookups (the single highest-leverage confirmation, collapsing the La Perla band, the wholesale swing factor, and per-store licensure at once), a census/ACS demographic refresh, a shift in Hispanic county share or Punjabi/South-Asian & Afghan migration, a Modesto ethnic-grocery or online-delivery change, an input-cost shock moving the ~5-10% chain gap, or a newly confirmed store changing the floor — that send the analysis back through the sizing and saturation nodes. Without this loop the 2026-06-30 snapshot silently goes stale as immigration rises and county Hispanic share climbs from 48.1% toward 50.0%.

cons.example: re-sizing the bands monthly when census shares and benchmarks move only yearly wastes effort

ignoring a fired trigger (new CDTFA/licensure data) and continuing on stale estimates

conflict_axes.name: demand_headroom_vs_licensing_and_leakage_gate
conflict_axes.description: A format can be demand-true white space yet be walled off by the licensing barrier stack or by Modesto/online leakage, so demand and feasibility point opposite ways.

conflict_axes.name: high_gross_vs_thin_net
conflict_axes.description: A meat-counter or bakery format shows a rich 25-45% gross while the sector net stays at ~1-3%, so a gross read and a profit read diverge.

conflict_axes.name: stacked_community_raiser_vs_four_caps

conflict_axes.name: commodity_basket_vs_specialty_middle

conflict_axes.resolution_hint: hold the 2026-06-30 snapshot as a dated baseline but let the review loop, not assumption, decide when migration has moved the equilibrium

edge_cases.description: A sub-category band is attached to a named business as if it were that business's actual revenue
edge_cases.trigger: a per-sub-category estimate is quoted next to a specific operator's name such as La Rancherita
edge_cases.mitigation: keep every band sub-category-level and estimate-not-actual; never bind a dollar figure to a named business as fact

edge_cases.description: The La Perla '$2M-$5M+' band migrates into prose as a stated fact
edge_cases.trigger: the multi-department outlier band is quoted without its lowest-confidence estimate tag
edge_cases.mitigation: keep the estimate tag and footprint-UNKNOWN flag on the band wherever it is reused and never lump it with the single-store carniceria band

edge_cases.description: The ~20,000 Assyrian community figure is quoted as a Census fact
edge_cases.trigger: the community estimate is used to justify three Middle-Eastern markets without its hedge
edge_cases.mitigation: keep the [FACT/ESTIMATE — community estimate] hedge wherever the ~20k figure is reused and cap the saturation read's confidence at that of the hedge

edge_cases.description: A high meat-counter gross (25-45%) is read as high net profit
edge_cases.trigger: a carniceria band's gross is taken as profitability without the owner-draw absorption
edge_cases.mitigation: pair every gross with the 1-3% net base case and the family-labor distortion before any profit read

edge_cases.description: The 8-12% operating/aspirational margin is quoted as a net margin
edge_cases.trigger: an ethnic-grocery KPI write-up's operating-margin figure is read as net
edge_cases.mitigation: treat 8-12% strictly as operating/aspirational, never net; the binding net read is ~1-3%

edge_cases.description: A commodity-basket-led store is recommended on demand alone
edge_cases.trigger: an entrant plans to win on staples (masa, produce, bulk rice) against the chains
edge_cases.mitigation: refuse commodity-led entry; the chain price floor and ~5-10% identical-goods cost gap doom it regardless of demand

edge_cases.description: Punjabi/South-Asian demand is read as fully capturable locally
edge_cases.trigger: the demand-side white-space is treated as open without the Modesto/online leak
edge_cases.mitigation: mark the opening contested: real unmet demand but a supply side partially pre-empted by out-of-town and online options

edge_cases.description: A bagged-tortilla or packaged-salsa wholesale lane is recommended without the PFR gate
edge_cases.trigger: a tortilleria wholesale-to-taqueria opening is judged on demand alone
edge_cases.mitigation: apply the CDPH Processed Food Registration packaging/distribution gate as an override before any wholesale yes

edge_cases.description: A straddle business is double-counted, inflating a sub-category's saturation
edge_cases.trigger: La Perla is tallied under carniceria and panaderia and tortilleria, or Shah under grocer and halal
edge_cases.mitigation: use primary category as the spine and let secondaries adjust effective coverage without double-counting the saturation read

edge_cases.description: The 10-count is asserted as a ceiling that rules out any further entry
edge_cases.trigger: a saturation conclusion is stated as proof that no eleventh ethnic grocer exists
edge_cases.mitigation: read coverage as a confirmed floor, leaving room for undercounted edge carnicerias and home-based/pop-up sellers

edge_cases.description: CDTFA receipts or a CDFA/PFR licensure lookup arrive and contradict the estimated bands and licensure inferences
edge_cases.trigger: measured retail sales-tax receipts or per-business licensure become available
edge_cases.mitigation: fire the review loop, replace the band/licensure estimates with the measured figures, and re-derive the per-sub-category read

workflow.description: Record the resident population, median income, age and the essential/cash demand character with cited magnitudes
workflow.gate: the resident base has public-fact magnitudes (pop ~72,888, income $82,995, age 34.9) and the cash/counter-cyclical character is named

workflow.action: Map the four stacked communities and the student layer
workflow.description: Tie each community and the CSU layer to the sub-categories they anchor, with the ~20k Assyrian hedge
workflow.gate: each of the four communities is tied to an anchored sub-category with its cited share and the ~20k Assyrian figure carries its community-estimate hedge

workflow.description: Record the primary/secondary straddles (La Perla, Shah, Turlock Halal Market, Nineveh, Halal Market and Food) and effective coverage
workflow.gate: the named straddles are recorded and the spine-is-primary-category convention is stated so coverage adjusts without double-counting

workflow.description: Derive each band as benchmark x size signal, paired with its cost/margin caveat
workflow.gate: every band is estimate-not-actual with a size signal, confidence, confirmation path and cost/margin pairing

workflow.action: Handle the La Perla outlier band
workflow.description: State the ~$2M-$5M+ multi-department band as the lowest-confidence figure, kept separate from single-store carnicerias
workflow.gate: the band is tagged lowest-confidence with footprint UNKNOWN and barred from migrating into prose as fact

workflow.action: Read the density and the why-ten equilibrium
workflow.description: Set ~1.37/10k against grocer-density benchmarks and resolve the stacking raiser against the four binding caps
workflow.gate: the four-stacked-communities raiser and all four caps are named and tied to the ~10-count outcome

workflow.description: Give the per-community ceiling per sub-category, including the Assyrian at-ceiling and the center-saturated/edge-open Mexican read
workflow.gate: each sub-category has a per-community ceiling read and the ceiling is flagged dynamic with the Hispanic-share driver

workflow.description: Trace the commodity leak to chains and the deep-specialty leak to Modesto/online, leaving the specialty middle
workflow.gate: both leakage directions are stated with the ~5-10% cost gap and the magnitude flagged UNKNOWN

workflow.action: Locate the specialty moat and contested white-space
workflow.description: Name the chain-proof moat and rank the contested openings each with its leakage/licensing qualifier
workflow.gate: the moat is named and at least four white-space openings are listed each with a leakage and/or licensing qualifier

workflow.description: Combine saturation, white-space, leakage, moat and the licensing stack into an open/avoid call
workflow.gate: the verdict names the do-not-open formats and refuses any demand-true but leakage- or licensing-gated addition

workflow.action: Set the market review cadence and triggers
workflow.description: Define the refresh cadence and material-change triggers routing back to sizing and saturation
workflow.gate: a cadence and a trigger list (CDTFA + CDFA/PFR licensure highest-leverage) routing to the sizing and saturation nodes exist

priority_rationale: The demand base, the four stacked communities, the student layer and the format straddles are foundational because every band, density and saturation read flows from them; the benchmark method precedes the per-sub-category bands, the La Perla outlier and the thin-net pairing it governs; density and the why-ten equilibrium build on the demand and straddle layers, then decompose into the Assyrian ceiling and the general per-community ceiling; competitive structure and the two-direction leakage feed the specialty moat and the contested white-space; the revenue-honesty guardrail and the coverage floor govern every dollar and count expression; and the entry verdict plus the review loop come last because they compose all upstream reads into a decision and a self-correcting refresh.

dominance_rules.rule: The revenue-honesty guardrail dominates any pressure for a single decisive number
dominance_rules.rationale: no per-business revenue, margin or footprint is public, so an over-decisive figure would be a fabrication
dominance_rules.trigger: a request for a named business's revenue or a single market number
dominance_rules.action: answer only with a labeled estimate (benchmark x size signal) plus method, source, confidence and confirmation path

dominance_rules.rule: The licensing barrier stack and leakage gate dominate a demand-true white-space opening
dominance_rules.rationale: the permit stack and Modesto/online leakage can make a high-demand format un-enterable
dominance_rules.trigger: a white-space opening is judged attractive on demand alone
dominance_rules.action: mark it a no-go until the licensing stack clears and the leakage test is passed

dominance_rules.rule: The 1-3% net margin dominates the high meat/bakery gross for any profit read
dominance_rules.rationale: the rich meat-department gross is absorbed by owner draw and thin grocery margins
dominance_rules.trigger: a high gross is used to characterize profitability
dominance_rules.action: replace it with the ~1-3% net base case and the family-labor distortion caveat

dominance_rules.rule: The specialty moat dominates the commodity basket for any entry rationale
dominance_rules.rationale: the commodity half leaks to chains at an unbeatable price floor
dominance_rules.trigger: an opening is justified on winning the staple basket
dominance_rules.action: refuse commodity-led entry and require the opening win on specialty, fresh meat, and in-house production

dominance_rules.rule: The hedged ~20k Assyrian estimate caps the Assyrian saturation read's confidence
dominance_rules.rationale: the three-market saturation call rests entirely on a community estimate, not a Census line
dominance_rules.trigger: the Assyrian saturation read is asserted at high confidence
dominance_rules.action: cap the read's confidence at that of the ~20k hedge and re-test if the estimate is revised

dominance_rules.rule: The coverage floor dominates any ceiling claim from the saturation reads
dominance_rules.rationale: the 10-count is confirmed, not a proof that no eleventh store exists
dominance_rules.trigger: a saturation read is stated as proof of no further entry
dominance_rules.action: frame the read as an at-least floor leaving room for undercounted edge/pop-up sellers

dominance_rules.rule: The La Perla outlier band dominates the single-store carniceria band for that business
dominance_rules.rationale: the multi-department supermarket is not comparable to a single-store carniceria
dominance_rules.trigger: La Perla is sized using the single-store carniceria band
dominance_rules.action: use the separate ~$2M-$5M+ lowest-confidence outlier band and never lump the two

dominance_rules.rule: A flagged low-confidence input dominates a confident downstream conclusion built on it
dominance_rules.rationale: a conclusion cannot be more certain than its weakest load-bearing input
dominance_rules.trigger: the La Perla band, the ~20k figure, or a leakage magnitude carries a conclusion above its own confidence
dominance_rules.action: cap the conclusion's confidence at that of its weakest input and name the confirmation source

dominance_rules.rule: Migration drift dominates the static snapshot for the per-community ceilings
dominance_rules.rationale: rising immigration and climbing Hispanic share move the ceilings the snapshot reads as fixed
dominance_rules.trigger: a per-community ceiling is treated as static
dominance_rules.action: route the read through the review loop when a migration or demographic trigger fires before re-asserting the ceiling

anti_rework_rules.rule: Map the four stacked communities before sizing any band or saturation read
anti_rework_rules.prevents: deriving bands and ceilings against a demand map that later moves, forcing a full re-derivation

anti_rework_rules.rule: Label every dollar figure estimate-not-actual with method, source and confidence at the moment it is written
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a later honesty sweep that must re-caveat figures already quoted as facts

anti_rework_rules.rule: Keep the La Perla outlier band separate and lowest-confidence the first time it is stated
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a single-store band contaminated by the multi-department outlier that must be re-split

anti_rework_rules.rule: Read saturation off primary category, noting straddles, before counting
anti_rework_rules.prevents: double-counted straddle businesses inflating a saturation read that must be re-tallied

anti_rework_rules.rule: Apply the licensing stack and leakage gate while ranking white-space, not after recommending it
anti_rework_rules.prevents: recommending an opening that the PFR/CDFA/halal gate or Modesto/online leak then voids

anti_rework_rules.rule: Attach the 1-3% net caveat to a revenue band when the band is built
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a high-gross band re-read as high profit that must be re-caveated downstream

anti_rework_rules.rule: Carry the ~20k Assyrian community-estimate hedge the first time the figure is used
anti_rework_rules.prevents: every downstream Assyrian saturation read inheriting an unhedged figure that must be re-marked

anti_rework_rules.rule: Name the CDTFA / CDFA-PFR confirmation path on every low-confidence dollar or licensure figure as it is stated
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a later pass to attach confirmation sources to numbers and licensure claims already published without them

anti_rework_rules.rule: State coverage as a floor the first time the 10-count is used in a saturation read
anti_rework_rules.prevents: ceiling claims that must be re-hedged once an undercounted store is confirmed

iteration_protocol.trigger: CDTFA / Turlock Finance retail sales-tax receipts and per-business CDFA/PFR licensure lookups become available
iteration_protocol.action: replace the revenue bands, the La Perla figure, the wholesale swing and the licensure inferences with measured figures and re-derive

iteration_protocol.trigger: a census/ACS demographic refresh or a revised Assyrian community estimate lands
iteration_protocol.action: re-run the community map and re-test the density and Assyrian saturation reads

iteration_protocol.trigger: Punjabi/South-Asian & Afghan migration or the Hispanic county share shifts materially
iteration_protocol.action: re-read the per-community ceilings and the contested white-space

iteration_protocol.trigger: a Modesto ethnic-grocery scene or national online-delivery change moves the out-of-town leak
iteration_protocol.action: re-estimate the deep-specialty leakage and re-qualify the South-Asian white-space

iteration_protocol.trigger: a chain (Walmart/FoodMaxx) pricing or input-cost shift moves the ~5-10% identical-goods gap
iteration_protocol.action: re-estimate the commodity leak and re-pair the revenue bands with refreshed cost reality

iteration_protocol.trigger: a store opens or closes in the catalog
iteration_protocol.action: re-tally the straddle-adjusted saturation reads and the per-community ceilings

iteration_protocol.trigger: a city/county/CDFA permit or PFR/halal-certification fee or availability changes
iteration_protocol.action: re-price the licensing barrier stack and re-issue any affected entry verdicts

iteration_protocol.trigger: a previously uncatalogued edge or pop-up seller is confirmed
iteration_protocol.action: update the coverage floor and re-frame the affected density and saturation reads
